findings.summary: The first discharge names HS53's status.json as its record, but the obligation text it quotes is in HS53's amendment.json. The README and the sibling v5 discharge both name amendment.json.
findings.evidence: status.json:60-64 has {record: architecture/host-interface-amendment-hs53/status.json, obligation: O-PROGRAMS-V3-OBSERVER, text: 'Republish the OBSERVER's two compiled programs ...'}. That text is byte-equal to the obligation in architecture/host-interface-amendment-hs53/amendment.json:314-317 (checked). HS53's status.json holds only the id, in its obligations list (:374); grep finds the text 0 times in status.json and once in amendment.json. README.md:17-18 says the obligation is in amendment.json. v5's status.json:14-15 discharges the sibling HS53 obligation O-SECCOMP-V5-OBSERVER-LISTENER with record amendment.json. The second v3 discharge (status.json:66-67) follows the v2 convention: the record is the file that holds the quoted text. The first breaks it, so a reader or mechanics check that follows the record cannot find the text. Fix: set record to architecture/host-interface-amendment-hs53/amendment.json. If the open-state list should also be cited, name HS53's status.json in a separate field.

findings.summary: As MET-ENFORCE-029's R1-1 found for v2: the checker follows symlinks and closes only programs/, not the rest of architecture/compiled-filter-programs-v3/.
findings.evidence: Tamper replay on a scratch copy (<scratch>/work, never the worktree). These all exit 1 with the expected message: a flipped byte in a v3 program; a truncated or appended instruction; a dotfile, subdirectory or missing program in programs/; a trailing space or changed field in index.json; a flipped byte in MET-ENFORCE-025's BROKER or OBSERVER program; a change to v5's vectors, the v5 model or MET-ENFORCE-029's index; an extra argument. Two cases exit 0: programs/OBSERVER.x86_64.bpf replaced by a symlink to identical bytes outside the tree (read_bytes and iterdir at :82, :139, :207-210 follow it), and a stray file in the v3 directory outside programs/. The committed state is correct: git ls-tree shows all nine new files as 100644 regular blobs. Carry this to the mechanics layer as in v2 (git modes and the complete file set of the directory).

findings.summary: The block layout is restated in the publisher, but the syscall numbers are not. They come from the pinned syscalls.json. v2 restated its block's number (BLOCK_AT) and checked it against the table.
findings.evidence: v2's BLOCK_AT = {aarch64: (34, 78), x86_64: (173, 267)} and its require(table[...]['nr'] == nr). v3's PAIR_AT/ACCEPT4_AT (:59-60) hold only indexes, and :143 reads bind/listen/accept4 from the table. The table is digest-pinned, so the check is equivalent, and the numbers are correct. syscalls.json gives x86_64 49/50/288 and aarch64 200/201/242. These match <research>/arch/x86/entry/syscalls/syscall_64.tbl:61,62,300 and <research>/scripts/syscall.tbl:244,245,288 (arch/arm64/tools/syscall_64.tbl in the tree is a link to it, stored as text). The README byte table restates them. The docstring line 'restated here instruction by instruction' (:17-19) is true of the opcodes, offsets and flag values only. Restating the six numbers, as v2 did, would make the publisher self-describing. This is optional.

The reviewer checked them independently (see checked). The mechanics layer needs to restate these checks: the 54 carried rows in order plus 2 new rows; the supersedes digest 89b47ef8...; ownerDecision, rules, notArtifacts and statuses equal to v5's; the four verbatim quotes across status.json, edge v6 and README; the two discharge texts; and the CANDIDATE and status-line states.

findings.summary: The replay paragraph starts 'The replay includes v5's 44 OBSERVER listener vectors' and goes on to describe plain accept and bind/listen with any arguments. v5 has no plain-accept OBSERVER vector, and its bind/listen vectors use only two argument sets per architecture.
findings.evidence: v5's vectors.json OBSERVER rows: 18 accept4, 2 bind and 2 listen per architecture (44 in all). The bind/listen args are all zero, plus (7, 0x7fff0000, 0x10) for bind and (7, 0x80) for listen. There are 0 rows with nr 43 (x86_64) or 202 (aarch64). Both statements are true of the published bytes. The reviewer's own interpreter shows: plain accept is KILL_PROCESS on both architectures; bind and listen are ALLOW under all-ones args, (3, 0x7fff0000, 110, 0x80000, 1, 2) and (2^63, 0, 0, 0x800). They are not vector-backed, though. Wording such as 'the published bytes also ...', or a plain-accept vector in a later allowlist revision, would make this exact.

findings.summary: Edge v6 labels the two lane-monitor messages 'Q-P2-MONITOR' and 'Q-P2-2-FACTS'. status.json uses the ids 'Q-P2-1..4' and 'Q-P2-2', and the READMEs use 'Q-P2-1, -3 and -4' and 'Q-P2-2'.
findings.evidence: The quoted texts are byte-identical across edge v6 (:624-625), status.json (:49, :55) and the unwrapped README block quotes (checked). Only the labels differ, and 'Q-P2-MONITOR' and 'Q-P2-2-FACTS' appear in no other file. Using status.json's ids in the edge strings would make cross-references exact. This is cosmetic.

For nr 0..1099 the new program equals the v5 model's policy oracle decide() everywhere. 11120 evaluations. PASS.

Kernel facts, from the local v6.12 research tree only. syscall_64.tbl: 43 accept, 49 bind, 50 listen, 288 accept4. scripts/syscall.tbl: 200 bind, 201 listen, 202 accept, 242 accept4. include/linux/net.h: SOCK_CLOEXEC = O_CLOEXEC, SOCK_NONBLOCK = O_NONBLOCK. asm-generic/fcntl.h: O_CLOEXEC 02000000 = 0x80000, O_NONBLOCK 04000 = 0x800 (arm64's fcntl.h includes it). x86 has no uapi fcntl.h in the tree, and asm-generic/Kbuild has mandatory-y fcntl.h. seccomp.h: struct seccomp_data with args[3] at offset 40 = 0x28, and populate_seccomp_data copies the 64-bit args. accept4 is SYSCALL_DEFINE4 with int flags, so the kernel ignores the high word, which matches the low-word rule. net/socket.c:1982 returns EINVAL for flags outside CLOEXEC|NONBLOCK. AUDIT_ARCH_* = EM_*|64BIT|LE, and RET_ALLOW/KILL_PROCESS and the BPF opcodes are confirmed. The tree is partial: elf-em.h (EM_X86_64 and EM_AARCH64 values) and x86's uapi fcntl.h are absent, so those values were not checked there.
